quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: When does alcohol start to impair your riding?

options.text: At about half the legal alcohol limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. You can be impaired below the legal blood alcohol limit. No amount of alcohol is safe before riding.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It includes specifications, operation, and maintenance information.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies partial rear braking when you use the front brake.
Applies partial front braking when you use the rear brake.
Applies equal braking to both front and rear brakes at the same time.
Remembers how hard you usually brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies partial front braking when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies partial front braking when you use the rear brake. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars tightly, slow down gradually by releasing the throttle, lean forward, and move to the side of the road. Avoid using brakes as they can also make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest and you operate it with your left foot. Lift the lever to shift up. Press it down to shift down.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: The same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It should not be used in curves.
It should use the shoulder when turning.

questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars handle curves differently than two-wheeled motorcycles.

questions.question: What should a passenger do while riding?

options.text: Lean the same way you lean.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way you lean.
questions.explanation: A passenger should lean with you through turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control, and hold onto the passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: How can you tell your rear tire has gone flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing noise from the rear.
The back end jerks from side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: When a rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. Riders rarely hear a tire fail.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the rear brake on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what road conditions you are on.

questions.question: What happens when a rear tire skids?

options.text: You lose the ability to change direction.
It is only dangerous if the front tire also skids.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose the ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash. When you apply too much rear brake pressure, the rear wheel locks up. Once this happens, you cannot change direction. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Make it easier for others to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you out of other drivers' blind spots and away from road hazards. It protects your lane, shows your intentions, and gives you an escape route.

questions.question: What should a good rain suit do?

options.text: Not puff up when you ride.
Not be needed because motorcycles should not ride in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not puff up when you ride.
questions.explanation: A good motorcycle rain suit resists tearing and does not puff up or balloon, even at high speeds.

questions.question: How much maintenance does a motorcycle need?

options.text: Only checks done by a mechanic.

questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle frequently. Do a complete check before every ride.

questions.question: What is the main psychoactive substance in marijuana?
questions.explanation: THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) is the main psychoactive substance in marijuana.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Losing traction on one or both wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, you may lose traction on one or both wheels and crash.
